content: # Haßloch. | Location of Haßloch within Bad Dürkheim district |. | Haßloch   is located in Germany Haßloch  Haßloch Show map of Germany  Haßloch   is located in Rhineland-Palatinate Haßloch  Haßloch Show map of Rhineland-Palatinate |. **Haßloch** (German pronunciation: ) is a large village in the Bad Dürkheim "Bad Dürkheim (district)") district in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. Haßloch is the Bad Dürkheim district's biggest municipality, exceeding even the namesake district seat. In 1689, it met the same fate again, more than once, in the Nine Years' War (known in Germany as the *Pfälzischer Erbfolgekrieg*, or War of the Palatine Succession), this time at the hands of the Spaniards and the French. In 1969, the old district of Neustadt an der Weinstraße was abolished and Haßloch was assigned to the newly created district of Bad Dürkheim "Bad Dürkheim (district)").

Last modified: **2023-02-16** by  klaus-michael schneider. ! image by *Jörg Majewski*, 7 May 2009. * County and Municipal Flags (Rhineland-Palatinate/ *Rheinland-Pfalz*). ## Haßloch Municipality. ### Haßloch Banner. Source: State Archive Speyer in *Klaus Günther*:"Kommunalflaggen von Rheinland-Pfalz", CD. ### Haßloch Coat of Arms. The draft of the arms was already made in 1926 but it took more than one decade, until the arms were approved. The lion is the representing the *Palatine Counts of Rhine*, the eagles are representing the *Counts of Leiningen*. The hook is shaped like amirrored initial "S" and is the proper local symbol, which can be found on local boundary stones.A court seal from the 18th centurx displayed the hook alone. The existence of flag and banner is proven since 1988. The arms were approved on 2 April 1938 by the governor in Bayern.

title: in english | Gemeindeverwaltung Haßloch
content: **“Richard Sang Collection“ a Unique Collection in Haßloch**. As of now, Germany’s only permanent exhibition of Suiseki-stones is on display at the Kulturviereck in Haßloch. Richard Sang, an entrepreneur from Haßloch, bequeathed the stones to the commune prior to his death. Richard Sang first became interested in the stones when he visited a Bonsai-exhibition in 1994. He then also wished for them to be exhibited in the Kulturviereck, which was not yet built at the time. When Sang’s wife died in 2016, the ownership of the stones was passed on to the commune, which then had to master the challenge of presenting them according to Richard Sang’s conception. Not only was it necessary to design an exhibition room at the Kulturviereck, but also to find someone who was familiar with this kind of art and could take care of the exhibition. Therefore, everyone who is interested is invited to get an idea of the “Richard Sang Collection” at the Kulturviereck in Haßloch.
